business_problem: Resilience needed a connected way to move lab and instrument data from multiple sites into the cloud so research teams could analyze results faster, back up data reliably, and integrate scientific information across the organization.
solution_summary: Resilience built a globally connected lab data mesh on AWS so scientists across sites can move instrument data to the cloud quickly and analyze it without manual transfer work. Data from on-premises laboratory systems is migrated by AWS DataSync and moved privately over AWS PrivateLink into Amazon S3, which serves as the centrally managed storage layer for both scientific and business users. At the edge, AWS IoT Greengrass automatically invokes migration tasks on demand, and AWS CDK is used to model the infrastructure as code so new devices and sites can be onboarded quickly. This architecture creates a shared data backbone across lab locations, integrates with internal and third-party analytics applications, and gives research teams near-real-time access to experimental data for faster learning cycles and more resilient data backup.

business_outcome: Resilience built the platform in less than 3 months, connected data from over 100 lab devices across six sites, uploaded more than 75 TB to Amazon S3, gives scientists cloud access in under 5 minutes, and can onboard new devices and entire sites in days.
